identity.title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment.

content.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition-associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type-specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type-enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.
